title: Profiling & torch.compile 🚄
description: Analyze performance bottlenecks and accelerate models with torch.compile.

slides.title: Finding Bottlenecks 🔍
slides.content:
# `torch.profiler`

PyTorch's profiler records GPU/CPU timing, memory usage, and kernel launches. Use it to find slow operations.

```python
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[...]) as prof:
    model(input)
print(prof.key_averages().table(sort_by='cuda_time_total'))
```
View traces in Chrome: `prof.export_chrome_trace('trace.json')`.

slides.title: Profiler Example
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch.profiler

model = nn.Conv2d(3,64,3).cuda()
input = torch.randn(8,3,224,224).cuda()
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
    model(input)
print(prof.key_averages().table(sort_by='cuda_time_total', row_limit=5))

quizData.question: What can torch.profiler show?

options.text: GPU time, CPU time, memory usage, and kernel names

quizData.explanation: The profiler provides detailed performance metrics for both CPU and GPU.

slides.title: torch.compile: The JIT Compiler 🧙
slides.content:
# PyTorch 2.0 Revolution

`torch.compile` speeds up models by analyzing Python bytecode and generating optimized kernels.

```python
model = torch.compile(model)
```
It works out‑of‑the‑box for most models. Backends: `'inductor'` (default), `'openxla'`, etc.

In many cases, 30‑200% speedup with no code change!

slides.title: Using torch.compile
slides.content: Compile a model for faster training/inference.
slides.codeSnippet:
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(100,200), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(200,10))
compiled = torch.compile(model)   # default backend 'inductor'
x = torch.randn(64, 100)
out = compiled(x)
print(out.shape)

quizData.question: What does `torch.compile` do?

options.text: Applies graph optimizations and generates efficient code, often speeding up execution

quizData.explanation: It optimizes the model's computation graph, reducing Python overhead and improving GPU utilization.

slides.title: Memory Optimization 🧹
slides.content:
## Gradient Checkpointing

Trade compute for memory by not storing intermediate activations. Recompute them during backward.

```python
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint
# inside forward:
x = checkpoint(self.block, x)
```
Useful for very deep networks.
